adventure.title: Scramble Ha Ling Peak
adventure.description: A relentless 800-metre climb straight up out of Canmore to a summit block where the whole Bow Valley drops away on three sides.
adventure.bonus: No sitting down until the summit.

adventure.title: Ice Walk Johnston Canyon
adventure.description: The same catwalks as summer, except the waterfalls are frozen solid into blue columns and you're walking on the creek in cleats.
adventure.bonus: Touch the frozen upper falls with a bare hand for five seconds.

adventure.title: Skate the Ice at Lake Louise
adventure.description: A cleared rink on a frozen glacial lake, with an ice castle in the middle and Victoria Glacier hanging above the far end.
adventure.bonus: Do one full lap of the rink backwards.

adventure.title: Canoe Moraine Lake at First Light
adventure.description: Push a canoe onto rock-flour blue water with the Valley of the Ten Peaks standing over you — the most photographed view in Canada, and worth every bit of the early start.
adventure.bonus: Stop paddling in the middle of the lake and drift in silence for five minutes.

adventure.title: Helicopter over the Rockies
adventure.description: Lift out of Canmore and fly the ridgelines and glacier fields of the front ranges — twenty minutes that recalibrate your sense of scale.
adventure.bonus: Sit up front and don't look at the camera once.

adventure.title: Snowshoe to Chester Lake
adventure.description: A gentle climb through spruce forest in Kananaskis to a frozen alpine lake ringed by peaks, with almost nobody else on the trail.
adventure.bonus: Bring a thermos and drink it standing on the frozen lake.

adventure.title: Larch Valley and Sentinel Pass
adventure.description: For three weeks each September the alpine larches turn gold, and this switchback climb above Moraine Lake is the best seat in the Rockies for it.
adventure.bonus: Make it all the way to Sentinel Pass, not just the meadow.

adventure.title: Float the Bow Through the City
adventure.description: Put in at Bowness Park and drift past the escarpments, the university and the downtown skyline on cold, fast glacial water.
adventure.bonus: Name every bridge you float under.

culture.title: The Calgary Stampede
culture.description: Ten days in July when the entire city puts on a hat and boots — rodeo, chuckwagon races, midway, free pancake breakfasts on every corner.
culture.bonus: Find a free pancake breakfast before 9am and eat at it.

culture.title: Contemporary Calgary in the Old Planetarium
culture.description: A brutalist 1967 science centre and dome theatre reborn as the city's contemporary art gallery — the building is half the exhibit.
culture.bonus: Stand in the middle of the dome and say something out loud.

culture.title: Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies
culture.description: Peter and Catharine Whyte's own paintings and the archive of the guides, climbers and Stoney Nakoda families who made these mountains legible.
culture.bonus: Find the oldest photograph on display and work out where it was taken.

culture.title: A Performance at Banff Centre
culture.description: One of the world's great artist residencies sits on Tunnel Mountain, and most nights something extraordinary is being premiered in its theatres.
culture.bonus: Go to whatever is on, without checking what it is first.

culture.title: Flames Game at the Saddledome
culture.description: The saddle-roofed 1988 Olympic arena, a sea of red, and hockey played at the volume Alberta thinks it should be played at.
culture.bonus: Join the C-of-Red chant without looking up the words first.

culture.title: Improv at the Loose Moose Theatre
culture.description: Keith Johnstone built Theatresports here, which means every improv show you've ever seen traces back to this room — Saturday night is still the best seat.
culture.bonus: Shout out the suggestion that gets used.

culture.title: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
culture.description: A UNESCO World Heritage cliff where Blackfoot people ran bison herds for nearly six thousand years, with an interpretive centre built into the hillside itself.
culture.bonus: Walk to the top of the jump before you go into the centre.

culture.title: The Banff Park Museum
culture.description: An 1903 log 'cathedral to nature' packed floor to ceiling with Victorian taxidermy — a perfectly preserved museum of how museums used to be.
culture.bonus: Find the specimen that has aged the worst.

8ball.title: Wildcard: The Icefields Parkway, No Plan
8ball.description: Drive 230 km of the most spectacular road in North America from Lake Louise toward Jasper, and stop at every pullout that looks good — no itinerary, no reservations.
8ball.bonus: Turn around at whatever time you agreed, wherever you happen to be.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Order the Strangest Thing on the Menu
8ball.description: Walk into the next restaurant you pass in Inglewood or Kensington and everyone orders the single item they understand the least.
8ball.bonus: Nobody is allowed to look it up before it arrives.

foodie.title: Wine Night at Bar Von Der Fels
foodie.description: A narrow, candlelit room with an obsessive natural wine list and small plates built to disappear alongside it.
foodie.bonus: Drink a grape variety you've never heard of.

foodie.title: Alberta Beef at CHARCUT Roast House
foodie.description: Rotisserie and charcuterie in the heart of downtown, doing the thing Alberta is actually famous for — beef — with real technique.
foodie.bonus: Order the cut you can't identify on the menu.

foodie.title: Distillery Dinner at Park, Banff
foodie.description: A working distillery on Banff Avenue using glacier water, serving campfire-cooked plates alongside its own gin and vodka.
foodie.bonus: Try the spirit you'd never order in a bottle shop.

foodie.title: Bakery Morning at Sidewalk Citizen
foodie.description: Sourdough, babka and pistachio croissants in the brick Simmons Building on the river — the best possible start to a Calgary morning.
foodie.bonus: Buy an extra loaf and give it to someone on the way out.

foodie.title: Dinner at Ten Foot Henry
foodie.description: Vegetable-forward sharing plates in a bright Beltline room — the restaurant that changed what Calgary expects from dinner.
foodie.bonus: Order the vegetable dish nobody at the table wants.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Deane House
foodie.description: A restored 1906 house at the confluence of the Bow and Elbow, cooking prairie ingredients with an Indigenous-informed hand and a superb patio.
foodie.bonus: Walk the riverbank behind the house before you sit down.

foodie.title: Fondue at The Grizzly House
foodie.description: A gloriously unchanged 1967 Banff fondue restaurant with rotary phones at every booth and exotic-meat hot rock plates — pure, committed kitsch.
foodie.bonus: Call another table on the booth phone.

foodie.title: Ramen at Shiki Menya
foodie.description: A tiny Bridgeland counter doing one thing extremely well — house-made noodles in a shio broth people queue in the snow for.
foodie.bonus: Finish the bowl before anyone else finishes theirs.

social.title: Après-Ski at the Rose & Crown
social.description: Banff's long-running upstairs pub with a rooftop patio, ski-boot crowds and live music most nights of the winter.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the first person who asks how your day on the hill was.

social.title: Live Music at the Palomino Smokehouse
social.description: Barbecue upstairs, a sweaty basement venue downstairs booking punk, country and everything between — the heart of Calgary's live scene.
social.bonus: Stay for the opener you've never heard of.

social.title: Beers at Cold Garden Beverage Company
social.description: Inglewood's least serious and most fun taproom — thrifted couches, board games, a dog on every third seat and genuinely good beer.
social.bonus: Win a board game against a stranger.

social.title: Cocktails at Proof
social.description: A dark, precise 1st Street bar that consistently lands on Canada's best-bar lists, with a rotating menu built like a concept album.
social.bonus: Order by describing a place, not a drink.

social.title: Speakeasy Cocktails at Betty Lou's Library
social.description: Knock at an unmarked door on 4th Street, give the password, and step into a book-lined prohibition room with a serious cocktail list.
social.bonus: Pick a book off the shelf and read one line aloud to the table.

social.title: Patio Evening on 17th Ave
social.description: Calgary treats patio season as a competitive sport — start at Craft Beer Market's rooftop and work your way along the strip.
social.bonus: Move to a different patio every drink.

social.title: Late Night at the Ship & Anchor
social.description: The 17th Avenue corner pub that has been Calgary's default meeting point for thirty years — patio in summer, packed in every season.
social.bonus: Make a plan with someone you meet there for the next day.

chill.title: Stargaze at Two Jack Lake
chill.description: Banff is a Dark Sky Preserve, and this quiet lake ten minutes from town gives you the Milky Way reflected in still water.
chill.bonus: Stay out long enough to see one shooting star.

chill.title: Cruise Lake Minnewanka
chill.description: An hour on Banff's largest lake, past the Devil's Gap and over a drowned resort town that still sits on the lakebed.
chill.bonus: Sit at the very back of the boat and don't move.

chill.title: Wander the Reader Rock Garden
chill.description: A terraced hillside garden laid out by a city parks superintendent a century ago, still holding thousands of species and almost no visitors.
chill.bonus: Find a plant you've never seen before and look it up after.

chill.title: Sunrise at Vermilion Lakes
chill.description: Five minutes from Banff Avenue, Mount Rundle turns pink over glassy water and you'll likely have a bench entirely to yourself.
chill.bonus: Get there before the first car does.

chill.title: Soak at the Kananaskis Nordic Spa
chill.description: Hot pools, cold plunges, eucalyptus steam and hammocks, all outdoors in a mountain valley — and phones are banned throughout.
chill.bonus: Do three full hot-to-cold cycles before you touch a hammock.

chill.title: Coffee and a Book in the Simmons Building
chill.description: Phil & Sebastian's flagship in a converted mattress factory on the Bow, with big windows, good light and coffee Calgary is genuinely proud of.
chill.bonus: Order the single origin and try to name a flavour note before you read the card.
